docs.title: 3D Cadastral Digital Twin & Cloud Pipeline
docs.text:
Automated end-to-end spatial ETL pipeline converting raw LiDAR point clouds and 2D building footprints into LoD1 CityJSON models and enterprise 3D streaming assets.

  • Python
  • PDAL
  • Laspy
  • CityJSON
  • PyVista
  • Cesium 3D Tiles
  • ArcGIS SLPK
  • glTF

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Manual 3D asset creation requires tedious desktop click-throughs and fails to scale when converting municipal LiDAR and flat 2D building footprints into interactive digital twins.

docs.title: Data & Technical Architecture
docs.text:
Follow the process. Expand a step for the details.

Pause animation
  1. 01 Raw LAZ Ingestion & Ground Filtering

    Ingested raw LAZ tile sets and 2D building vectors; executed automated ground classification and filtering via PDAL and Laspy.

    Details +
  2. 02 Normalized Height Extraction

    Programmatically computed building heights above ground by comparing rooftop Z-max values against ground surface models.

    Details +
  3. 03 CityJSON LoD1 Generation

    Serialized extracted building volumes into structured LoD1 3D CityJSON prisms using cjio.

    Details +
  4. 04 Geometry Validation & Compilation

    Ran automated mesh verification via PyVista (PLY/OBJ) and compiled assets into a unified spatial repository.

    Details +
  5. 05 Multi-Format Export

    Exported streaming-optimized formats including Cesium 3D Tiles, ArcGIS Scene Layers (.SLPK), and raw mesh packages.

    Details +

docs.title: Results & Impact
docs.text:
• Eliminated manual desktop bottlenecks, delivering a fully automated CLI-driven pipeline that scales 3D municipal asset production.
  • Successfully embedded an interactive web demo featuring real color-by-height/year-built styling and full attribute table interrogation.

docs.title: Cadastral Mapping Automation Guide (POC)
docs.text:
Automating bulk parcel mapbook production in ArcGIS Pro with ArcPy, from a Parquet parcel fabric to a multi-page PDF map series.

  • ArcPy
  • ArcGIS Pro
  • Map Series
  • Parcel Fabric
  • Cadastral Mapping

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Producing parcel map sheets by hand in ArcGIS Pro is slow and hard to repeat: each sheet has to be set up, checked and exported one by one, and scripts often break because of hardcoded file paths. This proof of concept automates the whole run. A single script reads the parcel fabric, drives a staged layout template, and exports every sheet into one PDF mapbook.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Follow the process. Expand a step for the details.

Pause animation
  1. 01 Parcel Data Preparation

    Converted the Parcels_2025 layer into parcel_fabric.parquet with pandas and PyArrow, stored under a relative path (../data/processed/) so the script runs on any machine.

    Details +
  2. 02 Layout Template Staging

    Built parcel_stage_template.aprx as the reusable layout: map frame, north arrow, scale bar, legend and the parcel information panel.

    Details +
  3. 03 Bulk Map Series Automation

    01_build_parcel_mapbook.py uses native ArcPy bindings to open the template, replace hardcoded paths with relative ones, and generate one map sheet per parcel.

    Details +
  4. 04 QC & PDF Mapbook Export

    Checked the cartographic vector layers on each sheet, then exported the full series as a single multi-page PDF mapbook.

    Details +

docs.title: Tools & Technologies
docs.text:
• ArcGIS Pro & ArcPy — layout template and map series automation
  • Python, pandas & PyArrow — reading and preparing the Parquet parcel fabric
  • Conda — isolated environment (prod-map-cadas-env)
  • Parquet — compact, fast storage for the parcel fabric

docs.title: Status & Next Steps
docs.text:
Status: In progress (last updated 2026-10-12).

  • Finish the cartographic QC of all layer components.
  • Move the layout to a web print template so map sheets can be produced from the browser.

docs.title: Maui Commute Traffic Hotspot Analyzer
docs.text:
Independent Case Study. A zero-cost spatial pipeline that fuses TomTom traffic flow data with OpenStreetMap road networks to flag the worst AM spillback intersections on Maui's Kula → Kahului commute.

  • Independent Project
  • Python
  • OSMnx
  • TomTom Flow API
  • Folium
  • GeoPandas
  • SQLite
  • APScheduler

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Maui's Kula → Kahului commute funnels through a handful of signalized intersections, but there was no quick, zero-cost way to see which ones actually cause the worst morning spillback. Commercial traffic APIs are expensive to query continuously, and raw OpenStreetMap road data carries no congestion signal on its own.

docs.title: Data & Technical Architecture
docs.text:
Follow the process. Expand a step for the details.

Pause animation
  1. 01 Road Network Ingestion

    Downloaded the OSM drive network for the demo area via OSMnx (~4,250 roads, 945 km) and cached it locally; each road is split into pieces of 250 m or less while keeping true road geometry, giving roughly 6,400 addressable segments.

    Details +
  2. 02 Scheduled Traffic Collection

    An APScheduler cron daemon sweeps the TomTom Flow Segment Data API across four daily windows (AM Peak, Midday, PM Peak, Weekend), rate-limited and cached in SQLite, staying well within the free tier's 2,500 requests/day. A deterministic synthetic mode generates the same data offline for testing, with no API key required.

    Details +
  3. 03 Spillback Detection

    Scanned every OSM-tagged signalized intersection in the network and, for each approach, walked backward against traffic counting contiguous congested road pieces; an intersection is flagged when its longest approach queue reaches the minimum threshold during the Weekday AM Peak.

    Details +
  4. 04 Interactive Map & Reporting

    Rendered a Folium map on a light basemap with a time-of-day slider, congestion-colored road segments, a floating legend, and spillback intersections marked with a hollow ring; auto-generated a top-10 hotspot markdown report and a congestion-index CSV alongside it.

    Details +

docs.title: Results & Impact
docs.text:
• Flagged 7 of 55 signalized intersections on the Kula–Kahului corridor as AM spillback hotspots, each identified by walking congested road pieces backward from the signal.
  • Built entirely on free-tier data — TomTom Flow Segment Data (2,500 requests/day) plus OpenStreetMap/OSMnx road geometry — at zero cost, no paid services.
  • A deterministic demo mode validates the full 945 km / ~4,250-road network offline, so the pipeline's bottleneck logic can be verified without any live API calls.

docs.title: Reality Capture Workflow
docs.text:
Deep learning land cover classification of drone and satellite imagery to map human activity and recreation pressure on Puerto Rico's coast.

  • Drone Imagery
  • Satellite Imagery
  • Deep Learning
  • Land Cover
  • ArcGIS Pro
  • Open Source

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Local government needed spatial evidence of anthropogenic activity and recreation pressure in Puerto Rico's coastal zone to support planning and resource preservation decisions.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Classify high-resolution satellite and drone imagery for each study area, choose the right land cover classes through data analysis, validate them with field data, and calculate the area of each class. The deliverables were a GIS layer for each area of interest, delivered as Shapefile or GeoJSON.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
• High-resolution satellite imagery
  • Drone (UAV) imagery
  • Field data for class validation
  • Coverage: coastal study areas in Puerto Rico, including ncón and La Parguera – Guánica

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
A hybrid workflow combining open-source tools and ArcGIS Pro, built around deep learning classification.

Follow the process. Expand a step for the details.

Pause animation
  1. 01 Imagery Input

    Collected high-resolution satellite and drone imagery for each study area as the raster input for the workflow.

    Details +
  2. 02 Segmentation & Class Design

    Split the imagery into segments and analyzed the data to decide which land cover classes to map.

    Details +
  3. 03 Deep Learning Classification

    Classified the segments with a deep learning methodology, combining open-source tools with ArcGIS Pro.

    Details +
  4. 04 Reclassification & QC

    Refined the first results through reclassification, validated the classes with field data, and checked integrity, completeness and agreed standards.

    Details +
  5. 05 Area Calculation & Export

    Calculated the area of each class, exported one GIS layer per area of interest as Shapefile or GeoJSON, and stored the results on the NAS server.

    Details +

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Completed the full segment workflow, from raster input to final vector output.
  • Classified and refined the segments, then validated them through quality control.
  • Delivered GIS layers for each area of interest as Shapefile or GeoJSON, ready for desktop and web GIS.
  • Stored the dataset in an organized folder structure on the NAS server for easy access.
  • Gave local government processed coastal land cover data to support planning and preservation decisions.
